tob-10088: The Epic of Gilgamesh, written on clay tablets more than four thousand years ago, is one of the oldest great stories in the world. It follows the proud king Gilgamesh of Uruk and his wild friend Enkidu on adventures that end in grief. The loss sends Gilgamesh on a quest for the secret of eternal life. The flood story it contains echoes the biblical tale of Noah.
tob-0144-54488: Anthropogenesis — volume two — gives Blavatsky’s secret history of man: seven root breeds from misty ghost-forms to ourselves, with Atlantis and Lemuria on the way. Wild as it seems, it fed bards, painters, and wonder-seekers for decades. The volume is Theosophy’s boldest flight.
tob-4185-79588: The fourth volume of Goodwin’s Plutarch gathers more of the Moralia — on heaven’s slow justice, on fortune, on music, and the famed talks on love. Here is Plutarch at his widest and kindliest. The edition’s steady Victorian prose keeps him a delight.
tob-9047-60688: Volume five of the Natural History spans metals, stones, and the crafts — delving, carving, painting, and Rome’s luxury trades. Pliny the preacher scolds his age’s wastefulness even as he lists it. The volume is a treasure-house of olden handiwork.
tob-0088: The Liber Juratus — Honorius’s Sworn Book — is a medieval wonder-book claiming high-church warrant for its rites of vision and spirit-raising. Laid to Honorius of Thebes, it vows the worker godly sights and bound spirits. Renaissance wonder-men prized the text.
tob-4188: E. B. Cowell’s Jataka strings the Buddha’s birth-tales of old — the Awakening-One as beast, king, and sage, teaching goodness by fable. His edition made these beloved stories open in English. The gathering is a treasure of Buddhist folk-tale. Bairns and scholars alike have loved these tales.
tob-10988: The Ladder of Jacob expands Jacob’s dream at Bethel — angels ascending and descending the ladder, with apocalyptic visions of Israel’s history. This Slavonic pseudepigraphon preserves otherwise lost Jewish traditions. The text is prized by scholars of early Jewish mysticism.
cia-0000105888: A February 1965 report on Sukarno's orders to harass American officials in Indonesia as a way to pressure Washington. The harassment was meant to push the United States into changing its policies toward Jakarta. The document shows diplomacy's rougher side: a leader using mistreatment of foreigners as a bargaining chip.
cia-0000107288: A June 1991 report in which an ambassador states that living American MIAs are unlikely to exist. Coming from a senior diplomat rather than an analyst, the judgment carried political weight in the long-running MIA debate. The document is one more official voice saying the painful truth: the missing were almost certainly gone.
cia-0000108488: Dated to an estimated January 1982, this document's title was deleted by censors — but the surviving fragment concerns an American priest murdered in Guatemala. The missing title cannot hide the subject: the killing of clergy in a dirty war. The redaction itself testifies to how sensitive the case remained.
cia-0000119588: An August 1966 report on plans for a Czechoslovak government delegation to visit North Vietnam. Prague was showing solidarity with Hanoi while quietly pursuing its own reforms. The document is a small tile in the mosaic of communist-bloc diplomacy during the Vietnam War.
cia-0000126888: A January 1968 report on a Soviet official's comments about the possible renewal of Arab-Israeli hostilities. Seven months after the Six-Day War, the next round was already being weighed. The document shows Moscow's men reading the Middle East's temperature — and Washington listening in.
cia-0000132188: Situation Report 505: Moscow denying it had military advisers in Iraq — the truncated title hints at more. The denial mattered because the advisers' presence would have meant Soviet complicity. The document captures the diplomacy of distance: an empire disowning its ally.
cia-0000132288: Situation Report 597: Iraq responding to something — the truncated title withholds the trigger. In the war's final days, every Iraqi move was scrutinized for signs of collapse or trickery. The entry is Baghdad's last maneuvers, watched closely.
cia-0000132488: An April 1960 report on Cuba increasing its ties with Communist China. Havana was diversifying its patrons — Moscow plus Beijing. The document spots the triangle: the island, playing the giants against each other.
cia-0000132588: A September 1960 report: Moscow attempting to exploit the Cuban situation. The Kremlin saw opportunity in the Caribbean crisis — a foothold in America's backyard. The document is the superpower, maneuvering: the opening, seized.
cia-0000135888: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on the compromise of PBSUCCESS. The operation was blown — or partly blown. The document is the disaster: the compromise, reported.
cia-0000136088: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LUGTON on black flights. Unmarked planes, secret missions. The document is the flight: the aircraft, unacknowledged.
cia-0000136188: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN on air raid warnings. The invasion's air war, anticipated. The document is the warning: the raids, expected.
cia-0000136288: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN stating justification for requesting broad authority to direct — the truncated title cuts off what. The power grab, defended. The document is the justification: the authority, argued.
un-sc-res-188: Security Council Resolution 188, adopted in 1964. The mid-sixties Council deliberated. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-688: Security Council Resolution 688, adopted in April 1991 — the Kurdish protection resolution, condemning Iraq's repression of its Kurdish population and demanding humanitarian access. It became the legal basis for the no-fly zones. The resolution is the shield: the Kurds, protected.
un-sc-res-1388: Security Council Resolution 1388, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The new year's Council deliberated. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1488: Security Council Resolution 1488, adopted in 2003 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1788: Security Council Resolution 1788, adopted in 2007 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1888: Security Council Resolution 1888, cataloged with the year 2008 — the historical record places this landmark sexual-violence resolution in September 2009, creating a special representative against wartime rape. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000135688: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135688. The exiles' paperwork, another set. The entry is the set: the documents, numbered.
cia-0000136688: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136688. The invasion year's documentation continued. The entry is the continuation: the documentation, unbroken.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d88: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 2, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 88. London answered the same day. The message is the quickness: the reply, immediate.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d188: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, November 4, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 188. Washington to London. The message is the link: the allies, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d288: A United States delegation memorandum, November 23, 1943 — Document 288. The American delegation's paper. The memo is the delegation's: the Americans, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d388: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, November 29, 1943 — Document 388. A second that day. The message is the doubling: the day, busy.
army-letters-from-an-officer-s-wife-1871: Frances Roe's letters home from frontier army posts paint a vivid woman's picture of the post-Civil War West — long marches, isolated forts, and encounters with a vanishing frontier. Candid and observant, they preserve daily life that official reports never captured. A gem of Western Americana.
the-history-of-australian-exploration-fr: Ernest Favenc tells the tale of a hundred years of trekking across Australia — from the first landing through Burke and Wills, Stuart, and the men who opened the vast inland. His story honors the grit and grief of the pathfinders. The best early record of how the lone continent was mapped and won.
arxiv-2605-08988: Machine-learned interatomic potentials predict how atoms push and pull, but do they generalize to arrangements never seen? Amir Masoud Nourollah, Irtaza Khalid, Stefano Leoni, and colleagues benchmark compositional generalization — combining known pieces in novel ways. The 2026 paper tests whether materials AI truly understands chemistry or just memorizes it.
arxiv-2605-09088: Stacking magnetic semiconductors atom-thin creates devices where electron spin and valley both matter. V. N. Mantsevich studies spin-dependent tunneling and intervalley scattering in such van der Waals stacks. The 2026 paper is condensed-matter theory for future spintronic devices.
arxiv-2605-09188: Reinforcement learners thrive on curricula — tasks neither too easy nor too hard — but grading difficulty is its own problem. Yang Zhou, Can Jin, Zihan Dong, and colleagues co-evolve the difficulty estimator alongside the learner in Dare. The 2026 paper teaches AI with a syllabus that writes itself.
arxiv-2605-09288: Elliptic PDEs — the equations of steady heat, electrostatics, and more — are expensive to solve finely. Ethan Hsu, Ivan Ge, and Hong Meng Yam speed them up with MC2: Monte Carlo correction for fast solving. The 2026 paper blends stochastic sampling with deterministic PDE solvers.
arxiv-2605-09688: Feedforward 3D Gaussian splatting is fast but flawed; diffusion priors can repair it — but only where they are confident. Rui Song, Tianhui Cai, Markus Gross, and colleagues learn the fixes with confidence-aware ConFixGS. The 2026 paper repairs 3D reconstructions intelligently.
arxiv-2605-09788: Symplectic log Kodaira dimension minus infinity marks the simplest symplectic manifolds; Hirzebruch-Jung strings resolve their singularities. Tian-Jun Li and Shengzhen Ning connect them to weighted projective spaces. The 2026 paper is beautiful symplectic geometry at its most classical and elegant.
plos-pone-0003388: Neuroscientists watched brains plan a grip in this 2008 imaging study. Volunteers grasped objects with either hand while scanners tracked the brain's grasp circuits, the areas that turn what the eye sees into hand movement. Activity shifted depending on which hand was used and whether the person was right- or left-handed, revealing how deeply handedness shapes motor planning.
plos-pone-0003488: Researchers tested an extra barrier against two common STIs in this 2008 clinical trial. Women using a diaphragm plus lubricant gel, on top of condoms, were compared with women using condoms alone for rates of chlamydia and gonorrhea. The results show whether adding the diaphragm and gel gave meaningful extra protection against cervical infections.
plos-pone-0003588: Reproductive biologists found the egg's skeleton controls its calcium in this 2008 study. Disturbing the cortical actin mesh of maturing oocytes scrambled calcium signaling, the trigger for single-sperm fertilization and embryo start. The result shows the cell's scaffolding is not passive architecture but an active director of fertilization.
plos-pone-0003688: In 2008, Dashtsoodol, Watarai, and Sakata found the thymus hiding unusual precursors. Alongside the known double-positive route, they identified double-negative cells that can become natural killer T cells. The extra precursor path widens the known family tree of these bridge cells between innate and adaptive immunity.
plos-pone-0003788: Schneider, Spitkovsky, and Riess built a sorter that frees stem cells from their nursemaids in this 2008 paper. Many stem cell lines need feeder cells to stay young, but the new technology separates the good cells into the pot and the feeders into the crop. The clean split gives labs pure stem cells without the helpers.
plos-pone-0003888: Back in 2008, Waldo and Scherrer produced a piece of the cell-division machine. Dad1p, part of the Dam1-DASH kinetochore complex, was made and characterized as a first step. The component work builds toward understanding how chromosomes get pulled apart.
plos-pone-0003988: In 2008, Egeland and Salas asked how well DNA databases cover rare types. Their methods estimated haplotype frequencies and database coverage for forensic genetic markers. The math matters whenever mitochondrial or Y-chromosome evidence goes to court. Better coverage estimates keep forensic DNA statistics honest inside the courtroom every day.
plos-pone-0004088: In 2008, Chang, Tang, and Ahmad found deafness starting at the cell doorway. Gap junction metabolite transfer in the cochlea broke down without connexin30. The inner ear's gap junction network faltered in the null mice. The work ties hearing loss to broken cell-to-cell supply lines.
plos-pone-0004188: In 2009, Serwanga, Shafer, and Pimego linked immune genes to slow HIV. Host HLA-B-linked Gag T-cell recognition tracked with slower HIV-1 disease. Broad multi-clade targeting marked the controllers. The pattern guides vaccine design toward Gag. The immune signature could steer future HIV vaccines.
plos-pone-0004288: In 2009, Malekzadeh, Alberti, and Nouraei blamed the fridge for Crohn's onset. Early exposure to domestic refrigeration linked to Crohn's disease risk. Cold-stored food may harbor the trigger. The hypothesis reframes a modern plague. The idea needs testing in prospective cohorts.
plos-pone-0357388: Some babies exposed to drugs or alcohol before birth are never reported to child protection — and little was known about how they fare. This study followed such infants for five years, tracking child-protection outcomes over time. The results show which families struggled and which stayed steady, guiding how hospitals and social workers spot at-risk infants early.
plos-pone-0358788: Public health can’t fight HIV without knowing how many men who have sex with men are on campuses. This cross-sectional study estimated the population size in Hainan colleges using a geographical social network app. The numbers give health workers a realistic base for prevention programs.
plos-pone-0358688: When a player takes a head knock on live TV, millions watch how it’s handled. This study asked how the public perceives concussion in live sport broadcasts — the commentary, the replays, the return-to-play decisions. The perceptions it captured shape pressure on leagues to take head injuries seriously.
plos-pone-0357888: Can wishing others well ease your own pain? This randomized controlled trial assessed loving-kindness meditation’s effect on pain and social well-being. The rigorous design tests whether this gentle, ancient practice delivers measurable relief — for the body as well as the social heart.
plos-pone-0357288: Hospital pneumonias caused by drug-resistant bacteria are every doctor’s nightmare. This subgroup analysis tested imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam against hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia from imipenem-nonsusceptible pathogens. The results guide last-resort antibiotic choices when standard drugs fail.
plos-pone-0358588: Guardrails must stop speeding cars without becoming spears themselves. This paper presented lightweight design and post-impact stability analysis of an extra-high grade guardrail built from 700L high-strength steel. The stronger steel means lighter rails that still hold firm on impact — safer roads for less material.
plos-pone-0357988: Uzbekistan’s local apples need defenses against fire blight, powdery mildew, and apple scab. This paper used marker-assisted screening to hunt resistance genes in local varieties. The genetic markers it found will speed breeding of hardier orchards adapted to Central Asian conditions.
plos-pone-0345688: Salty, sodic soils strangle the sugar fields of Ethiopia’s Metehara estate. This paper evaluated phosphogypsum applications and pore-volume water rates for reclaiming saline-sodic cambisols there. The reclamation recipe offers a tested path back to productive fields for one of the country’s key agricultural zones.
plos-pone-0356888: A traditional Chinese herbal formula may hide synergistic anti-aging compounds modern science hasn’t mapped. This paper used artificial intelligence to identify and mechanistically explore those compounds in the Dengzhan Shengmai formulation. The AI-driven approach bridges ancient medicine and modern molecular biology.
plos-pone-0326588: Roadside trees silently catch traffic pollution on their leaves — a free air-filtering service. PPDRTL is a novel framework for predicting pollutant deposition on roadside tree leaves using linear regression. The model quantifies how much grime urban trees actually trap, giving planners numbers for green infrastructure.
plos-pone-0357488: Lifting straps change what athletes’ muscles actually produce. This study measured the influence of lifting straps on force, rate of force development, and impulse during isometric mid-thigh pulls in judo and resistance-trained athletes. The evidence tells coaches and lifters what straps really do — beyond gym lore.
plos-pone-0356688: Common vetch — Vicia sativa — feeds livestock across climates, but its nutritional quality shifts with the weather. This paper studied that variation across climatic gradients and developed a comprehensive forage quality index. The index helps farmers feed animals better, whatever the climate.
plos-pone-0356788: Tuberculosis still kills over a million people yearly — and needs a far better vaccine. This in silico framework designs and validates a multi-stage subunit TB vaccine using a reverse vaccinology approach. The computational design accelerates vaccine development without waiting for slow trial-and-error.
plos-pone-0357088: Rubber-modified asphalt must survive years of heat and oxygen assault. This paper investigated the thermo-oxidative aging properties and mechanisms of high-content desulfurized rubber modified asphalt, from macro-rheological to micro-chemical perspectives. The insights point toward longer-lasting pavements.
plos-pone-0356988: In the Yangtze River Delta’s counties, people and land urbanize at different speeds — and the mismatch matters. This paper traced the spatiotemporal evolution and stage-driven mechanisms of population-land urbanization coupling coordination. The analysis reveals where urbanization is balanced and where it’s flying apart.
plos-pone-0355688: Tritrichomonas foetus — a sexually transmitted cattle parasite — infects many animal species, but how many? This paper published a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of its global prevalence across species. The planned synthesis will produce the first comprehensive picture of this costly pathogen’s reach.
plos-pone-0356488: Elderly patients with bile duct stones face risky surgery — but there’s a gentler way through. This paper reported percutaneous transhepatic cholangioscopy-guided holmium laser lithotripsy for bile duct stones in elderly patients. The minimally invasive technique shatters stones without the trauma of open surgery.
plos-pone-0356088: Marine mammals carry their own staphylococci — and Southern California’s are unmapped. This paper studied the diversity among Staphylococcus intermedius group isolates from Pacific marine mammals. The bacterial census informs both wildlife health and the zoonotic risks facing humans who share the coast.
plos-pone-0356388: Pointing accurately — toward a seen target — is fundamental to neurological exams. This paper evaluated a new clinical test protocol for pointing acuity in an initial validity study. The validated protocol gives clinicians a standardized way to measure a deceptively simple ability.
plos-pone-0355988: Running outside costs more energy than treadmill running — even at a 1% incline. This paper compared running economy, oxygen cost of transport, and energy cost between overground and treadmill running. The findings matter for every runner who assumes treadmill fitness transfers perfectly to the road.
plos-pone-0355488: Lipedema — a painful fat disorder — devastates women’s quality of life and body image. Sweden’s LISE study compared affected women against healthy controls and women with cancer. The stark comparisons validate suffering that medicine has long dismissed — and demand better care for a neglected condition.
plos-pone-0355188: Coal gangue — mining waste — can become cement’s ally when properly activated. This paper studied cement composites using composite-activated coal gangue. The findings turn an environmental liability into a construction resource — building with what mines discard.
plos-pone-0347188: Sleep disturbances erode quality of life — and Qassim, Saudi Arabia’s rates were unmapped. This paper measured their prevalence and association with quality of life in the general population. The findings give Saudi health planners the data to treat sleep as the public health issue it is.
plos-pone-0355288: Detecting sparse malaria parasites — low-density Plasmodium falciparum — pushes qPCR to its limits. This paper showed magnetic bead-based enhancement improves detection rates, comparing nucleic acid extraction methods. The improved sensitivity catches infections that standard methods miss — critical for elimination campaigns.
plos-pone-0354288: Wind erosion threatens Eastern Iran’s soils — and susceptibility varies across the landscape. This paper modeled that susceptibility using machine learning. The ML maps tell land managers where the wind will steal the soil next — so defenses go up in time.
europmc-pmc2845588: Astaxanthin, the pigment that pinks up salmon, may also tune human immunity. This 2010 trial finds it decreased oxidative stress and inflammation while enhancing immune response in people. The authors measure the effects directly in human volunteers. The study gave the supplement claim a real clinical test.
europmc-pmc2873288: Short chromosome caps may doom lungs. This 2010 paper links telomere lengths and TERT gene changes to pulmonary fibrosis, a scarring lung disease. The authors show patients carry shorter telomeres and harmful mutations. Their finding tied the biology of aging to a deadly lung illness, hinting that telomere tests could flag at-risk people.
europmc-pmc2876988: The brain chemical dopamine does more than signal pleasure; it tracks value and risk. This 2010 review by Wolfram Schultz gathers basic and recent data on dopamine's role in reward and risk signals. The author's synthesis shaped how neuroscientists think about choice. The review remains a landmark in decision science.
europmc-pmc2892488: Aligning many genomes means tracking gains, losses, and shuffles. This 2010 paper introduces progressiveMauve for lining up many genomes at once, even when chunks have moved. The authors' tool handles the chaos of rearranged DNA. Their software became a staple for comparing bacterial genomes.
europmc-pmc2920088: The nonstick chemical PFOA needed a health reckoning, and this 2010 paper gives it. The authors sift human studies of PFOA's toll on bodies. Their roundup ties it to sundry harms. The review fed new rules. Regulators leaned on its findings when setting drinking-water limits.
europmc-pmc2944788: Why do DNA predictions work for some traits but not others? This 2010 cattle study examines genetic architecture of complex traits and genomic prediction accuracy, using coat color, milk fat, and type as contrasting models. The authors' comparison clarifies the rules. Their work refined breeding math.
europmc-pmc2945788: Big biology data needs shareable workflows anyone can rerun. This 2010 paper introduces Galaxy, a web workbench for open, repeatable life-science computing. The authors' platform puts analysis in every browser. Their tool became a bioinformatics staple worldwide. Labs everywhere adopted it for teaching and research.
europmc-pmc6550188: An AI that screens eyes for diabetic retinopathy - without a doctor in the loop - passed its pivotal trial. Tested in primary-care offices, the autonomous system matched specialist-level detection of the sight-threatening disease. The FDA authorized it, a first for fully autonomous AI diagnosis, promising cheaper and wider screening for people with diabetes.
europmc-pmc6595688: PKM2 is a metabolic switch with a split personality: quiet in most adult tissues, loud in embryos, healing wounds, and - notoriously - cancers. This review covers the enzyme's many jobs in sugar metabolism, how cells dial it up or down, and why tumors love it. The M2 form of pyruvate kinase sits at a crossroads of growth and disease.
europmc-pmc6696688: Medical students - tomorrow's doctors - suffer striking rates of anxiety, yet it goes undertreated. This meta-analysis pooled global studies to measure how widespread the problem is. The numbers argue for treating healers' mental health as seriously as their training.
europmc-pmc6701588: Reactive oxygen species are cellular exhaust - useful in small puffs, toxic in clouds. This review compares ROS production and antioxidant defenses in healthy versus malignant cells. Cancer's altered redox balance, the authors show, is both a vulnerability and a shield.
europmc-pmc6723188: Alpha-lipoic acid - a sulfur-containing compound our own cells make - doubles as an antioxidant drug. This review surveys its therapeutic uses, from diabetic nerve pain to broader protective roles. The evidence backs a modest molecule with an outsized resume.
europmc-pmc6751188: Light is the body's timekeeper - dawn tells the brain when to wake, dusk when to wind down. This review explains how light sculpts circadian rhythms, sleep, and mood through the eye-brain pathway. In an age of midnight screens, the science matters more than ever.
europmc-pmc6752088: Hunger, eviction, no ride to the clinic - social needs shape health as surely as germs. This study measured how often US health systems screen patients for food insecurity, housing instability, utility and transport needs, and violence. The gaps show medicine still treats bodies while missing lives.
europmc-pmc6778088: Belly fat is the dangerous kind - and gut microbes may predict who carries it. This study linked the Blautia genus to visceral fat accumulation in adults aged 20 to 76. The microbial fingerprint could flag at-risk bodies before the scale does.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-88: This 2007 GAO report finds the anthrax shot program repeating its own mistakes — shaky buys of a new vaccine and sloppy care of the licensed stock on hand. The nation's germ-defense shelves deserved better buying discipline, GAO argues. The report is a plea to run biodefense like lives depend on it, because they do.
gao-gaoreports-b-299888: Accent Service Company took its contract dispute to GAO in 2007, and this ruling settles it for good. The firm challenged the agency's award as unfair; the call weighs the protest point by point and rules. Quiet, workmanlike, binding — the everyday machinery of keeping federal buying fair for all.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-888: Hanford's toxic billions needed a tighter leash in 2007 — GAO's report says the Energy Department had to toughen its watch over contractor payouts at the waste plant. The findings target the money valves of the priciest cleanup on earth. When the bill runs to the billions, the report argues, the purse strings cannot dangle.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-388: The Pentagon's weapons shopping needed a portfolio brain in 2007 — GAO's report says managing the investments as one portfolio would sharpen the buying. The findings make the business case. The report's pitch: run the arsenal like a fund, not a flea market.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-88: Housing the next catastrophe's victims needed a plan in 2007, and GAO's report says better planning was essential for sheltering the displaced. The findings demand the playbook. The report warns that the tents and trailers should not be improvised again. The next storm would not wait for the plan.
gao-gaoreports-b-299088: Alutiiq Global Solutions doubled its February 2007 protest — two case numbers, one services fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Paired filings get one careful answer. Two dockets, one fair verdict.
openalex-w7205006588: For patients with non-ischemic heart failure, sudden cardiac death is a leading killer, and implantable defibrillators are the main defense. This literature review evaluates how well these devices prevent sudden death in that population. The authors weigh the evidence for using the implant as primary prevention. A focused cardiology review that helps doctors and patients decide when the device is worth it.
openalex-w7205006988: Marcelo Caetano's 2024 film Baby follows Wellington, fresh out of juvenile detention, and Ronaldo, a young sex worker, through the streets of Sao Paulo. This review reads the film through queer theory, examining how it portrays gay life in the urban margins. The author treats the movie as both art and social document. A sharp piece of film criticism for readers interested in Brazilian cinema and queer storytelling.
openalex-w7204947088: Acne is often dismissed as a teen phase, but its marks run deeper than skin. This narrative review looks at how common acne affects the mental and social lives of teenagers and young adults. The authors gather research on self-image, anxiety, and daily life beyond the pimples themselves. A reminder that a skin condition can be a psychological burden, and deserves to be treated as one.
openalex-w7204635388: More children are being diagnosed on the autism spectrum, and small-town schools feel the pressure. This study asks teachers in Dom Inocencio, Piaui, what difficulties they face including autistic students. The authors document the gap between the duty to include and the tools teachers have. Honest and local, it shows inclusion as a daily struggle in one municipal school system.
openalex-w7204485688: The maker movement says students learn by building, and this article brings that spirit to biology and chemistry class. The authors study the promise and the pitfalls of maker methods for science teaching: hands-on projects replacing dry lectures. The research asks what changes when students make instead of memorize. An inviting look at classrooms as workshops.
openalex-w7162264588: Rumors fight like viruses, and this paper models the battle. The authors propose a mathematical model for competing rumors, such as fake news versus its correction, where each side's spread shifts public opinion. They capture the two-way dance between contagion and belief. A timely study of the epidemiology of lies.
openalex-w7137857988: Hunting new antibiotics starts with screening thousands of candidates fast. This paper proposes Euglena gracilis, a single-celled alga, as a high-throughput platform for antibacterial testing. The authors built the screening system. A methods study speeding the search for tomorrow's drugs.
openalex-w7129093688: Lung cancer too advanced for surgery still has radiation options. This review traces three decades of radiation therapy advances for unresectable locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer. The authors charted the evolution of treatment. An oncology review of progress against a tough foe.
pmc-13456788: A 2026 retrospective study building a model to predict early corneal swelling after phacoemulsification, the standard cataract surgery. Corneal edema can cloud vision after the operation, and predicting it from pre-surgery data lets surgeons plan safer procedures. The model turns routine records into a practical warning tool.
pmc-13443488: This 2026 cancer paper shows that the ATF4/SCO2 pathway blocks ferroptosis — an iron-driven form of cell death — in lung cancer by activating MAPK signaling. Tumors exploit the pathway to survive what should kill them. Mapping the escape route identifies targets for drugs that force cancer cells into ferroptosis.
pmc-13434188: A 2026 plant biology perspective asking a delightful question: how do plants survive without adaptive immunity — the tailored antibody defenses animals have? The author surveys the alternative strategies plants evolved. It is a clear, big-picture essay on the ingenuity of plant defense.
pmc-13451088: This 2026 review offers translational perspectives on immunotherapy targets, germline cancer syndromes, and newly discovered gene fusions. "Translational" means bridging lab findings to patient care, and the paper connects inherited risk, immune targets, and fusion genes into one clinical picture. It is aimed at oncologists moving new biology into treatment.
pmc-13401088: In this 2026 study, researchers examined how maternal stressors and social support in early pregnancy relate to stillbirth risk among fetuses with birth defects, exploring effect modification. The interaction between stress, support, and vulnerability is the focus. The findings speak to prenatal care for high-risk pregnancies.
pmc-13454688: A 2026 evolution paper showing that autopolyploidy — doubling the genome — shifted the species niche of Saxifraga oppositifolia from sexual to vegetative reproduction. Whole-genome duplication rewrote the plant's life strategy. The niche shift is evolution in action.
pmc-13554388: This 2026 cardiac surgery paper examined optimal timing of surgery and prognostic factors for heart attack complicated by ventricular septal rupture — a catastrophic tear. Timing is everything in this emergency. The analysis guides the impossible decision.
pmc-13509388: In this 2026 MRI paper, a shape-conforming high-density posterior cushion coil improved SNR and image quality in pediatric MRI. Comfortable coils make better pictures of squirming kids. The design is the advance.
pmc-13467188: A 2026 retrospective MRI case-control study linking lower trochlear facet asymmetry ratio to objective patellar instability in patients with patella alta. The bony shape predicted the dislocating kneecap. The ratio is a new imaging marker.
pmc-13487388: A 2026 real-world study of first-line palbociclib for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer in women aged 75 and older (the title is truncated). The elderly need their own data. The feasibility study provides it.
pmc-13421088: A 2026 systematic review of clinical and diagnostic considerations in laryngeal leishmaniasis — the parasite infecting the voice box. The rare presentation is easily missed. The review gathers the diagnostic wisdom.
pmc-13423888: This 2026 paper showed DNA extracted from aged formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded specimens of papillary thyroid carcinoma patients can be used for whole exome sequencing. Old pathology blocks hold genomic secrets. The validation unlocks archives.
